industries.narrative: Broad E&P participation with 89% advancing and +1.72% cap-weighted move, but relative volume is anemic — price strength lacks institutional conviction.

sector_breadth_notes.note: Energy strength is concentrated in E&P names; broad participation across 36 tickers suggests a commodity/crude-driven bid rather than idiosyncratic single-name moves.
Materials sector qualifies at the ETF level but internals are ugly — Gold, Steel, and Other Industrial Metals all in laggard bucket with near-zero advancers. Sector move is not organic.

Industrials show sharp internal weakness: Airlines, Electrical Equipment, and Metal Fabrication all sub-1.3 scores with zero-to-minimal breadth. Sector qualification masks broad industry deterioration.
Health Information Services collapsing (4.5% advancing) despite sector qualifying — points to defensive pharma/device leadership rather than growth-oriented healthcare tech.
Travel Services zero-breadth laggard drags on discretionary; sector strength must be coming from retail/autos/homebuilders rather than reopening/experience names.

key_divergences: Massive divergence: 10 sectors qualify at ETF level but only Oil & Gas E&P clears industry gate. Materials qualifies while Gold/Steel/Metals all rank as worst laggards — sector-level breadth is misleading and driven by narrow cap-weighted leadership.
leadership_theme: Energy E&P is the sole conviction industry; broad sector qualification masks weak internal breadth
